title: Catastrophic Co-op Search
content:
I have been having the most miserable and agonizing co-op search this semester guys. Over 100 applications as a COS undergrad. At this point in my search I have landed 0 interviews.

I visit the Career Design Studio often, I've reworked my resume countless times, but I have 0 results or feedback to work off of. Just the occasional rejection email that coincidentally comes out the second I see one of my peers accept the job on linkedin. Every day it takes all of my strength to keep holding on and keep myself from quitting. It's so hard and I feel like I have no reason to keep going. I have a great GPA for COS, I have completed a co-op already, and I'm an interesting candidate if you ask me. But my grand total of 9 (Yes 9) rejections out of the \~130 applications I've sent is just infantilizing and demoralizing. It's straight up making me depressed

title: Depressing Co-op search
content:
I feel like we’re all commiserating on here about our difficult co-op searches so I figured I’d share mine too! 

I’m rising fifth year Marketing major with two co-ops under my belt. I assumed landing a third would not be as difficult as it has been.

It feels pretty late in the process to be landing so few interviews and having little communication from employers. If I’m having as hard a time as I am with my age and prior co-ops, I can’t imagine how difficult it is for the younger students with one or no co-ops. 

Honestly, my frustration is with the university and co-op program. We need to stop admitting so many students and for new relationships with employers to have more co-op slots open. We all came to the school for this reason and it’s such a headache for all of us!!

Just wanted to share my situation and that even with two co-ops complete completed I’m still having a hard time.

title: Fall to spring co-op switch for accounting major?
content:
Would love any advice from accounting upperclassmen/alumni!

**Context:**

* Rising sophomore, accounting concentration, 5 year/3 co-op plan
* Currently on fall co-op cycle, considering switching to spring
* Did freshman year at Oakland so extracurriculars are not that strong (no accounting clubs/orgs, no boston networking yet)
* 3.83 GPA
* Coming back to Boston this fall
* Long term goal is big 4 audit then eventually FP&A

**Why I'm thinking about switching:**

From what I've read, spring cycle lines up with big 4 audit busy season, which is when firms hire more and co-ops actually get substantive work. Fall cycle is during audit shoulder season with fewer slots and less aligned with how big 4 recruits. Recruiting timelines also seem to be better for spring since postings drop in aug/sept of sophomore year.

However, if I switch, I'm in recruiting \~4 months from now with basically zero accounting related extracurriculars from my time at Oakland. BUSN 1103 slots also close soon for fall, so the decision is essentially due in the next week or two before it's too late.

**What I'm trying to figure out:**

* Is spring actually that much better for accounting/big 4 at neu? Would love to hear from anyone who's done either cycle, especially accounting specifically.
* Realistically, what are the odds of landing a big 4 co-op with a thin resume? Are midtier/regional firms the more realistic target? I'd take midtier but just want to know what I'm actually playing for instead of going in delusional.

Would appreciate any advice. Thanks!

title: Running out of Claude credits? Mahoraga is here.
content:
Northeastern gives us 300 a month, 500 if you're lucky, and premium seats if you're really lucky. By no means is that a small amount; it really is a useful resource that all students should honestly be abusing. (not to cheat on your NUpath courses, but to learn!) 

However tokens are getting more expensive, models are heavier, and i know a bunch of kids that run out before the end of the month. they wait for northeastern, but there are a million students here, and they just can't give us more and more. I personally use claude in my co-op as well, which eats usage. 

"So just use a local model," a smart freshman kid would say. local models run on your own device, and are essentially free. However cloud models like claude, chatgpt, most mainstream subscription models are just smarter and logically sound. 

I built **Mahoraga**, which routes simple tasks using contextual bandits (LinUCB) to local models to cut costs, as well as increase speed. Most work you do consists of bash, edit, etc. honestly pretty quick and light commands that claude really shouldn't have to run. All local inference, all free. Cloud escalation exists but only fires on retry.

So if you're doing CS/Business/honestly whatever nowadays and want to build/ship more often this might be the solution. Clone the repo, fork the repo, everything is **opensource** so you can use claude to implement this if you run into difficulty. Runs on your computer, no one else gets the data except you. (not me, not northeastern). 

Fork, Clone, Star, Steal: [github.com/pockanoodles/Mahoraga](https://github.com/pockanoodles/Mahoraga)

I ran 192 tasks across 8 agents (4 local Ollama models, 4 cloud CLIs) on a 16GB MacBook Pro, forcing round-robin so every agent got every prompt. Quality is scored by a 4-layer heuristic system (novelty ratio, structural checks, embedding similarity, length ratio). Zero API cost for evaluation, and no LLM-as-judge.

Results, tables, and analysis is on the github. If you study CS/DS/AI, you probably know more than me. Input would be appreciated.

title: Recent NEU grad — was it worth it? Honest question for current students/alumni
content:
Ever since I graduated, everyone keeps asking me if Northeastern was worth it. Honestly it's a loaded question for me personally because I'm heading back home for a family business, so my path looks different from most.

But I have cousins who are seriously considering NEU for the co-op program and before they commit I wanted to get a real pulse check from people who've lived it.

Would you make the same choice if you were deciding 4 years ago?

From what I've seen in my friend group, most don't have jobs lined up yet, but almost all of them are still glad they went. The exposure, the co-ops, the network it seems like it counts for something even when the job market is rough.

Not looking for a sales pitch either way, just genuine retrospectives. What would you tell your pre-frosh self?
